svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Receptors and ligands work like a lock and key."], [1, "Wrong shape: it does not fit the binding site."], [4, "Right shape but wrong charges: repelled, no binding."], [7, "The ligand: complementary shape AND chemistry. It binds."], [9, "Binding changes the receptor's shape and triggers a response inside the cell."], [11.5, "Only cells with the right receptor respond."]]
svg.title: Receptor and ligand: lock and key
svg.desc: A membrane receptor with a binding site: a wrongly shaped molecule does not fit, a correctly shaped molecule with repelling charges does not bind, and the specific ligand fits like a key, changing the receptor shape and triggering a response; only target cells with the receptor respond.
svg.text: Receptor and ligand: a lock and key

g.data-info: A protein, here in the plasma membrane, with a binding site for one specific signalling chemical.
Its shape and chemical properties (such as charges) are complementary to one ligand only: like a lock.
A molecule with the wrong shape cannot fit the binding site, so it does not bind.
Right shape, but its charges repel those in the binding site, so it does not bind either.
The specific signalling chemical. Shape and charges are both complementary, so it binds.
Binding changes the shape of the receptor, which triggers a response inside the cell.

g.text: response inside the cell, e.g. an enzyme activated

g.data-info: A cell responds to a signal only if it has the receptor for it.
